note: Paraphrased rule records with section-level citations for the Golden Loan Path (Fannie conventional, W-2 base income, depository assets, DU). Each record names the section and an anchor phrase that must exist in the privately cached official text for the regression step to pass. A rule is usable only while its section revision is ACTIVE on this install.

rules.text: A stable and predictable flow of income is foundational; the lender verifies stability, history of receipt, and reasonable expectation of continuance.

Income with a defined expiration date must be documented as expected to continue for at least three years from the note date; income with no defined expiration and the required history may be treated as continuing unless there is knowledge to the contrary.
DU indicates the minimum income verification documentation required; if stability cannot be determined from that documentation the loan must be resubmitted to DU with the correct information.

The most recent paystub must be dated no earlier than 30 days before the initial loan application date, include all year-to-date earnings, and be complete, legible, and computer-generated or typed by the employer (or downloaded from the employer's site).

W-2 forms must cover the most recent one- or two-year period required for the income type and clearly identify the borrower as the employee; the most recent W-2 is the one for the calendar year before the current calendar year. An IRS Wage and Income Transcript, Form 1005, or final year-to-date paystub are acceptable alternatives.
Paystubs and verification documents must comply with the allowable age of credit documents in B1-1-03.
When employment is validated through the DU validation service, the lender is not required to obtain the standard employment verification documentation.
The lender evaluates employment for a reliable pattern over the most recent two years; a shorter history may be acceptable with offsetting positive factors.
Employment gaps during the most recent 12 months may indicate unstable employment; frequent job changes with consistent, predictable income are acceptable.

A future pay raise may be used only for fixed base income on a purchase or limited cash-out refinance when it takes effect within 60 days of the note date, is fully verified by the employer, and the employer is not a family member or interested party.

Base income is regular earnings independent of overtime or bonuses. Fixed base income is a set salary or a fixed hourly rate with guaranteed minimum hours; variable base income is a fixed hourly rate with fluctuating hours or an hourly rate that varies.
For fixed and variable base income: a completed Form 1005 or the most recent paystub and most recent W-2, plus a verbal VOE.
Fixed base income has no minimum history requirement for inclusion as qualifying income; continuance need not be verified unless there is reason to believe it may not continue.
Variable base income requires a minimum 12-month history of receipt.
Monthly income by pay frequency: annual gross / 12; monthly gross as-is; twice-monthly gross x 2; biweekly gross x 26 / 12; weekly gross x 52 / 12; hourly gross x average hours per week x 52 / 12.

Variable base income, stable or increasing trend: average year-to-date and previous year's earnings over the months covered; the calculation must include at least 12 months of income. Decreasing trend: confirm the income has stabilized after the decline, otherwise it is not eligible; calculate as year-to-date income divided by months elapsed in the current year.
Average hours method: average monthly hours over at least the most recent 12 months multiplied by the current fixed hourly rate.
Qualifying income must be consistent with year-to-date base earnings; if year-to-date income reflects fewer than 30 days of earnings, confirm consistency with the prior year's earnings.
Pay raises for variable base income must be in place before closing.
Bonus, commission, overtime and tip income: a two-year history is recommended; a history of no less than 12 months may be acceptable with offsetting positive factors.
Documentation: a completed Form 1005, or the most recent paystub and two years' W-2s, plus a verbal VOE.

Compare year-to-date to previous years; stable or increasing: average year-to-date and previous year's earnings over the months covered (minimum 12 months); decreasing: confirm stabilization, otherwise not eligible.
A verbal verification of employment is required for each employed borrower (see the section for timing relative to the note date and acceptable third-party alternatives).

Assets may be verified by Form 1006 (VOD), bank or investment statements, retirement statements, lender-produced printouts, or a third-party asset verification vendor. All statements must clearly identify the financial institution, identify the borrower as the account holder, include at least the last four digits of the account number, the time period covered, all deposit and withdrawal transactions (depository accounts), and the ending account balance.

Purchase transactions: statements for the most recent full two-month period (or most recent quarter if reported quarterly). Refinance transactions: the most recent full one-month period. If the latest statement is more than 45 days before the application, obtain supplemental bank-generated documentation.

Funds in checking, savings, money market, certificate of deposit or other depository accounts may be used for the down payment, closing costs and financial reserves; the funds must be verified as described in B3-4.2-01.
A large deposit is a single deposit that exceeds 50% of the total monthly qualifying income for the loan.
rules.anchor: 50% of the total monthly qualifying income

rules.text: Purchase: if the large deposit is needed to complete the transaction, document its source; verified funds must be reduced by any undocumented portion. Refinance: documentation of large deposits is not required, but the lender must still identify borrowed funds and related liabilities. When part of a deposit is documented, only the unsourced portion counts against the threshold.
Reserves are measured in months of the qualifying PITIA payment for the subject mortgage, from liquid financial assets.

For DU loans there is no minimum reserve requirement for one-unit principal residence transactions; DU determines reserves for other occupancy/property types (for example two months for second homes, six months for 2-4 unit principal residences and investment properties).

Credit documents (credit reports and employment, income and asset documentation) may be no more than four months old on the note date; for consecutive statements the most recent one controls; older documents must be updated.

Resubmit the casefile to DU when the recalculated DTI exceeds 45% or increases by 3 percentage points or more (for example when verified income is less than the application income or new debts are disclosed).

Resubmit when verified reserves are less than 90% of the Reserves Required to be Verified, or when actual funds required to close exceed the DU findings amount without sufficient documented liquid assets.

The DU Underwriting Findings report states the recommendation, eligibility, and casefile-specific verification messages; the level of documentation DU recommends may not be adequate for every borrower and situation, and potential red-flag messages do not change the recommendation.
